tiers.name: A second pitch beside the first

events.line: A coach party wandered through the Guildhall Market and cleared your table.
Rain drove half of Bath indoors and into the market.
The Christmas shoppers came in waves. You ran out of string.
A power cut shut the hall for the day. Your cakes stayed put.
Someone set up a stall of cakes next to yours. The cakes were shop-bought and everybody knew it.
Local radio mentioned your stall by name. You were not warned.

upgrades.name: A card reader
upgrades.text: Nobody carries cash. The fees are the price of being easy to pay.

upgrades.name: Standing orders from the tea rooms
upgrades.text: A steady order every week, and a bad week stings less.

upgrades.name: An evening pitch at the fairs
upgrades.text: More people, later, with a good deal more to spend. Someone has to mind the stall in the dark.

asks.title: A pitch at the Christmas market
asks.text: A pitch at the Christmas market has come free, because someone else's cakes went wrong, and the organiser has asked {deed} if it wants it.

options.label: Take it and bake all week
options.say: Twelve hours a day in a woolly hat, selling cake to people in better hats. A triumph.

risk.say: A warm spell, no crowds, and a great deal of cake.

options.label: Take it for the weekends only
options.say: Weekends are busy and the weekdays are yours.

options.label: Say thanks but no
options.say: Someone else takes it and does well.
